title: EU-only routing enforcement, customer allowlist/denylist, and residency guarantees
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a policy-driven routing layer that enforces EU-only data residency for customers that require it, supports customer-level allowlists and denylists for regions/endpoints, and ensures fallback model variants preserve residency guarantees. The feature must apply consistently across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployment modes and emit audit records for compliance verification.
acceptance_criteria: Policy service evaluates request metadata and returns a routing decision (region tag + allowed endpoint classes) within 5ms p95
Requests for customers with EU-only residency flag are routed exclusively to EU-hosted endpoints or on-prem/VPC equivalents; no traffic leaves EU regions for these requests
Customer allowlist/denylist is enforced: denied regions return 403 with a clear error code; allowlisted regions are preferred even if outside the low-latency route
Fallback behavior: when primary EU model variant is unavailable, router only selects fallback variants that are explicitly tagged as 'EU-compatible' to avoid residency violations
Audit log contains immutable entries for every policy decision with fields: request_id, customer_id, decision, selected_endpoint, model_variant, timestamp
Integration tests cover hosted, dedicated, and private permutations and simulate cross-region capacity failures to validate safe fallback
Console shows per-customer residency status and routing decisions in the observability dashboard for at least 30 days
notes_or_decisions: Decision: Enforce residency at the routing layer (policy service) rather than at downstream model servers to centralize compliance checks and simplify auditability.
Trade-off: Central policy checks add ~2-6ms overhead; mitigated by caching policy decisions for short TTLs keyed by customer+route fingerprint.

Model tagging: Require model onboarding to include 'regional_compat' tags (e.g., EU, US) and a 'residency_safe' boolean; the router will reject variants without tags when servicing residency-restricted customers.

Private/Dedicated nuance: For Dedicated and Private customers we prefer customer-managed endpoints when present. If a Dedicated pool is in EU, it satisfies EU-only customers; if not, we will not route to Dedicated outside EU for those customers.
Security: All audit logs must be written to customer-scoped, immutable log stores with KMS encryption and retention policy configurable by PM/Legal.
Metrics: Expose 'residency_policy_decision' counters and latency histograms to SLO dashboards; add alert when % of policy cache misses exceeds threshold.

Fallback policy: Do not automatically route across legal boundaries for availability; instead return a structured error and follow configured customer fallback policy (allow-fallback, block, or manual-override).
Edge case: For hybrid requests (some data stored in EU, some in other regions), default to safest behavior (treat as EU-only) and route accordingly; document in runbook.
